Past analyses of AAPL (most recent first):

[2026-09-21 | AAPL | Underweight | -0.2% | +0.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AAPL: trim 25–30% of a full-weight position into the 339.64–342.90 resistance stack using limit orders scaled around 340.00 (30–35% only if the position is oversized or the risk budget is already strained), leaving a 70–75% core — do not exit, do not short, and do not initiate new exposure at 338.98. The 344.60 level is a rebuild/invalidation reference, not a protective stop; the residual core's real line is a daily close below the 50-SMA at 320.62, with a further cut there and a medium-term bull-case break on a close below 305.49. Reserve 15–20% of standard allocation: at most 5–7.5% may be deployed on a stabilized pullback into 328–332 with a stop below 320.62 (not 323.50, which is under one ATR from a 324 fill), with the bulk held for post-Q4 confirmation of gross margin ≥49.5%, converting inventory, and an explained $12.1B intangible / $13.5B noncurrent liability build. Size the residual so a repeat of the 2026-07-31 −7.36% gap on 132.5M shares is survivable without forced action; horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 print.

**Investment Thesis**: DIRECTION: the trim wins narrowly but clearly; the size and the reload ladder are what the debate actually contested, and that is where I rule.

What is not in dispute. All three risk seats, the Research Manager and the trader converge on reducing exposure from 338.98. Not one seat defended full-weight holding at the wall, and the neutral seat's "wait for confirmation with 100% exposure is not neutral — it is a directional long with no additional risk control" is the decisive framing. The bear case on current price risk/reward is arithmetic, not opinion: ~1.65% to the 344.57 record against ATR of 7.256 points (2.14% of price), five stacked resistance levels (339.64 21-Sep high, 340.08 record close, 342.75–342.89 upper band/July high, 344.57 record), ~5.4% to the 50-SMA at 320.62 and ~11.3% to the August low. You are being paid less than one day's noise to hold through a resistance test.

Where the aggressive seat wins and where it overreaches. It wins the tape: the push into the wall came on 35.0M shares versus a 43.1M average (0.81x), the MACD histogram has decayed 2.028 → 1.613 (−20.5%) while price rose 3.28%, MFI is 74.1 and %B 0.899, and the 2026-09-18 session absorbed 86.6M shares yet closed only at the 60th percentile of its range after tagging 338.49. That last print is the closest thing to a failed test this chart offers, and it is the specific evidence that distinguishes this trim from the ones this desk has been punished for. But the aggressive seat is wrong on two counts. First, "the trade to avoid" in the research applies to new money at 338.98, not to existing ownership: the report's own distribution is 55% breakout continuation / 30% rejection / 15% trend failure. RSI 66.32 is not overbought, the MACD line is positive at 5.930, the histogram is still positive, closes have held above the 10 EMA at 331.57 since 2026-09-10, and 5.73% extension over the 50-SMA versus 9.59% at the July peak means more support underneath, not less. Second, its "high-conviction asymmetric tactical top" with a fast reload at 324–332 is a directional bet dressed as risk management — if the Q4 inventory and margin picture is messy, 324–332 does not hold.

Where the conservative seat wins and where it overreaches. It wins execution: limit orders into 339.64–342.75 rather than a market sell at 338.98, a 30–35% trim at the upper end of the range, no short, and the correct insistence that 344.60 is an invalidation/re-entry reference rather than a protective stop on a long trim. It also wins the stop-geometry point the neutral seat seconded — a stop under 323.50 from a 324 fill is less than one ATR and is noise-stop territory; the honest line is the 50-SMA at 320.62. Its gap-risk logic is adopted outright: the 2026-07-31 −7.36% session on 132.5M shares proves stops do not stop gaps, and the only control that works is size. Where it overreaches is the blanket ban on any pre-event reserve deployment. The desk's own log (08-19, 08-26, 09-09) records that gated adds below a rising tape repeatedly never fill and forfeit the move; a conditional, ATR-stopped small tranche at genuine support is not the same error as chasing.

The construction adopted is therefore the neutral seat's, hardened by the conservative seat's arithmetic and freed from the aggressive seat's reload sprint. Trim 25–30% into 339.64–342.90, core 70–75%, reserve 15–20% with at most 5–7.5% releasable on a stabilization signal inside 328–332 and stop below 320.62, the bulk behind the Q4 gates, and no full-size re-risk on a first close above 342.90 — the core participates, and any add requires volume >43M with the histogram back above 2.03 plus preferably a held retest, stop 335.40.

THE PRIOR-LESSON PROBLEM, ADDRESSED HEAD-ON. This desk's record is emphatic that AAPL Underweights inside intact uptrends have cost alpha repeatedly — 07-13, 07-20–07-24, 08-12, 08-13, 08-17, 08-20, 08-21, 08-24, 08-27 and 09-02 each forfeited roughly 1.5–5.5% of five-day alpha, and 09-08 at $316.22 cost +5.9%; the 09-11 reflection concluded that entry-price discomfort must not be relabeled as ownership risk without a failed retest or a stop breach. Three things distinguish this case. (1) There is now an absorption/failed-thrust print into resistance — 09-18's 86.6M shares closing at the 60th percentile of the range — which the earlier trims did not have; they were made at triple-tested support on momentum decay alone. (2) This is a trim into a five-level resistance stack inside a 1.65% window, not a cut at support. (3) It is not one seat's discomfort: all three independent seats, the Research Manager and the trader land on 25–35%, so this is corroboration, not the single-seat relabeling the 09-11 lesson warns against. And the residual is 70–75%, not the 45% the 09-08 decision cut to — the cost of being wrong on an intact 28.7%-EPS-growth franchise is bounded, with the core fully participating in a breakout.

The fundamental caution is a gate, not a veto. Q3 FY2026 gross margin 50.06%, EPS $2.02 +28.7%, nine-month FCF $110.2B +52.5%, net cash $62.2B and a current ratio above 1.0x are a high-quality asset and the reason this is not Sell. Against that, the unresolved items are real and land in the same late-October window as the trim: inventory +94%, raw materials +260%, finished goods −4.1%, net intangibles +$12.1B and other non-current liabilities +$13.5B with no acquisition line to explain it, plus a 37–42x mechanical P/E and thinning volume. The fundamentals report itself says sizing should assume an information event on inventory at the Q4 call. That is precisely what a 25–30% trim sized ahead of the event is for.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT. Upgrade to Hold/Overweight on a daily close above 342.90 then 344.57 on volume above 43M with the MACD histogram re-expanding above 2.03 and a held retest, restoring toward standard weight; or on a Q4 print with gross margin ≥49.5%, inventory flat-to-down rather than writing down, revenue growth holding double digits, and the $12.1B intangible and $13.5B noncurrent liability build clearly explained. Downgrade to Sell on a daily close below the 50-SMA at 320.62 (cut further), a close below 305.49 (medium-term bull case broken), gross margin below 48% with decelerating revenue, an inventory write-down, or a quantified liability from the UK collective action or BASF suit.

STATED GAPS. No portfolio context, so every figure is a fraction of the caller's own standard AAPL allocation and must respect their single-name limits. No options chain or implied volatility, so no collar or put spread into the late-October print can be priced — event risk must be managed through gross exposure. No segment, product, geographic, unit or ASP disclosure, so 50.06% gross-margin durability is unattributable on both sides. No consensus forward EPS and no peer multiple set, so the 37–42x figure is mechanical and unverified; every cited level here is technical, not valuation-derived. The tape figures are internally inconsistent across seats (a 35.0M-share, 0.81x-average approach versus an 86.6M-share 09-18 session), which I resolve by treating the 09-18 absorption as the confirming print while holding the volume gate at 43M. No sentiment, positioning or insider-transaction data. The cause of the 2026-07-31 −7.36%/132.5M-share gap remains unestablished.

**Price Target**: 328.0

**Time Horizon**: 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
Over the five sessions the raw return was −0.2% but alpha vs SPY was +0.8%, so AAPL modestly outperformed the benchmark and the Underweight tilt did not earn relative alpha; the window is far shorter than the 1–3 month thesis and too short to judge it. That undercuts the “trim wins narrowly but clearly” price-risk/reward claim at the 339.64–342.90 resistance stack, while leaving the core-holding and event-gating logic around the Q4 inventory/margin print and the 320.62 line untested. Lesson: do not score an Underweight trim on five-day relative alpha alone—predefine the evaluation window and require either a failed retest, a stop breach, or the Q4 gate before changing size.

[2026-09-18 | AAPL | Overweight | +1.5% | +0.2% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AAPL, but build it in tranches and do not pay up at the 336.13 quote. First tranche: a half-size limit of roughly 3% of a standard AAPL allocation in the 329.92–332.53 zone (10 EMA / 9-18 low), tactical stop 324.90, with a time-based fallback of ~2% at market if that zone never prints within roughly five sessions while price holds above the 10 EMA — the logged non-fill error that has repeatedly left this desk under-owned in an intact AAPL uptrend. Second ~3% only on a daily close above 340.08 on above-average non-expiration volume with a hold/retest (ideally MACD histogram >1.63); final ~4–6% only on Q4/FY2026 confirmation, capping pre-Q4 exposure at 105–110% of standard allocation and 115–120% only after that confirmation. Risk controls: pause all adds on a daily close below 329.92, cut tactical tranches below 326.37, reduce to benchmark on a daily close below 320.14, size each tranche so a 2×ATR (~14.6 points, to ~315.3) costs 0.25–0.5% of portfolio, and avoid margin given AAPL's four −3.6% to −7.4% single-session drops in 2026.

**Investment Thesis**: DIRECTION IS SETTLED; ENTRY GEOMETRY AND PRE-Q4 SIZE ARE THE DISPUTED QUESTIONS — which is why this is Overweight, not Buy and not Hold.

What the aggressive seat won, and neither opponent rebutted with a number: the operating engine and the primary trend. 9M FY26 revenue $364.4B, +16.2% YoY; Q3 revenue $109.4B, +16.4%; Q3 gross margin 50.06% (+356 bps); Q3 operating margin 32.62%; Q3 EPS $2.02, +28.7%; 9M EPS $6.88, +22.4%; 9M FCF $110.2B; net cash $62.2B; debt/equity 0.78x. Incremental Q3 gross margin of ~71.9% and incremental operating margin of ~48.7% show real operating leverage, not a one-off. Structure corroborates: 336.13 > 10 EMA 329.92 > 50 SMA 320.14 > 200 SMA 286.34, with the 200 SMA rising monotonically; the 50 SMA flattened 7/30–8/17 and re-sloped to ~+0.50 pts/session; MACD 5.517 vs a 3.915 signal with the histogram positive at +1.603 after a full negative-to-positive reset; RSI 64.25, not overbought, with no bearish divergence at the 9/17–9/18 highs; price +2.99% above a VWMA (326.37) that has risen ten straight sessions; and the entire 310.69–333.43 July gap zone recovered. The conservative seat conceded the franchise and the trend and never dented either. That is why neither Hold nor Underweight survives — and this desk's own record is explicit about the cost of the alternative: Underweights on 07-13, 07-20–07-24, 08-11–08-13, 08-17, 08-20, 08-21, 08-24, 08-27, 08-28 and 09-02 each forfeited roughly 1.6–5.5% of five-day alpha inside an intact uptrend, while the 08-26, 09-04, 09-09, 09-10 and 09-11 overweights/holds earned +3.2% to +5.4%.

What the conservative and neutral seats won, and why not Buy: the entry price, the gap asymmetry, and the binary ahead. From 336.13 there is ~2.5% to the prior high but ~4.8% to the 50 SMA, so the plan's 3:1 only exists at a retest or a confirmed breakout. The resistance is a stack, not a line: 338.49 (intraday high), 340.08 (July closing high), 341.01 (Bollinger upper band), 344.57 (July intraday high). Extension is real: ~17.4% above the 200 SMA, and the 9/18 session's 86.59M shares (~2.1× the ~41.2M 19-session average) was third-Friday expiration-distorted and closed −0.26% below its open as a rejection of 338.49. RSI pushes above 70 into this 338–344 zone preceded two 2026 drawdowns; the MACD histogram flattened (1.625 → 1.538 → 1.603) while price pressed supply. The conservative seat's gap point is the strongest single rebuttal to the aggressive case and it is arithmetic, not sentiment: a 324.90 stop is only ~1.52%, i.e. inside one ATR of 7.31, and AAPL has already printed four −3.6% to −7.4% single-session drops in 2026 (including −7.35% on 132.5M shares on 7/31). A tight stop is not protection against a gap. Quality-of-earnings caution also stands unrebutted: 9M opex +21.9% against revenue +16.2%, R&D +32.3% in Q3, the 9M tax rate up 219 bps to 17.58%, OCF growth of 43.1% helped by ~$10.8B of lower cash taxes, ~$14.6B of working-capital swings and capex down 28.2%, Q3 OCF growth decelerating to 23.3% from H1's 53.3%, inventory +94% (raw materials +260%, finished goods −4%), intangibles +91% to $25.4B, and a $13.5B rise in other non-current liabilities with no footnote. Those are unresolved facts, not bull pillars.

Where each seat overreached. The aggressive seat is right that the plan does not buy at 336.13, but wrong to wave off both the stop geometry and the fact that this would be a pre-committed 115–120% overweight into a binary Q4 print; "aggressive risk management" is still an overweight before confirmation. The conservative seat is right on gap risk and right to demand a risk budget expressed in portfolio terms, but capping AAPL at 100–105% and requiring a 340.08 close plus a retest plus Q4 evidence before meaningful exposure converts a genuine uncertainty into paralysis, and its own reflection log shows where that error lands. The neutral construction is the one that survives, and I adopt it with two refinements drawn from this desk's mistakes.

The construction. Target 115–120% of a standard AAPL allocation, but cap aggregate exposure at 105–110% pre-Q4. Tranche 1 is half the plan's size — ~3% of standard allocation — a limit in 329.92–332.53 (10 EMA to the 9/18 low), tactical stop 324.90 (below the VWMA 326.37 and roughly 1.5×ATR), sized so a gap to 320 or 315 is survivable rather than assuming a clean stop fill. Refinement one: because the 09-01, 09-04 and 09-09 reflections all record that a tranche placed 2–3% below a rising tape simply never fills, add a time-based fallback — if the zone does not print within roughly five sessions while price holds the 10 EMA, take ~2% of standard allocation at market rather than forfeiting participation. Tranche 2, ~3%, only on a daily close above 340.08 on above-average, non-expiration volume, ideally with the MACD histogram above 1.63, followed by a hold or retest; if AAPL gaps through 344.57, wait for the retest rather than paying the gap.
